summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted for vomiting and altered mental status. She was diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis, a Klebsiella pneumoniae urinary tract infection, and hypertensive urgency. She was treated in the ICU with an insulin drip and IV fluids to resolve DKA, and antibiotics with meropenem for the UTI. Her blood pressure was managed with IV labetalol and transitioned to oral lisinopril and metoprolol. Phantom limb pain was controlled with gabapentin and morphine. Her mental status improved, and she was stabilized on subcutaneous insulin. A kidney ultrasound showed chronic parenchymal disease, and a CT chest revealed chronic lung changes without acute findings. She completed treatment, had negative blood cultures, and was discharged home with services for continued care.
